_comment: The canonical admin URL per Instatic site — the single answer to 'what link do I send?'.
`adminUrl` is the origin a person should work from; `check-origins.mjs` appends its www/apex
twin automatically, so list only what that would not derive: a second client domain, the
platform host, staging, an old domain people still have bookmarked.
List a host even when it is currently broken — a host nobody checks is a host nobody fixes,
and the checker's job is to keep saying so until it is clean.
This file is the claim; `node check-origins.mjs --all` is the proof, and it probes the RUNNING
server rather than the Railway dashboard. Re-run it after any domain change or redeploy and
fix whichever of the two is wrong.
No secrets here. Credentials live in the per-worktree .env and never in this repo.
A `<client>-staging` entry is that client's staging instance; tools/instatic-plugins reads production and staging hosts from here (2026-09-23).

sites.note: Fixed 2026-08-28: www.drnahlah.com and drnahlah.com appended to PUBLIC_ORIGIN, which already held encorercm.com + www + the railway host from the 2026-08-18 fix. drnahlah.com 301s to www, so www is the one that must be listed. All five origins verified live.

Fixed 2026-08-28. PUBLIC_ORIGIN had been set to the apex alone (https://masonparkdental.com) and had NEVER been applied — the container was still running its boot-time derived value. The apex also has no DNS record, so it is listed for the day it gets one but is not the link to hand out. Redeployed; www now verified live.

Domain cutover 2026-09-22: brandklout.ai and www.brandklout.ai are both attached in Railway and Cloudflare-proxied, certificates valid, and both already served the site — but PUBLIC_ORIGIN was still the railway host alone, so both were TRAP hosts. Now https://brandklout.ai,https://www.brandklout.ai,https://brandklout-production.up.railway.app; redeployed (a127e9f6) and all three verified OK. www is a separate Railway customDomain reading REQUIRES_UPDATE because its CNAME is proxied by Cloudflare; it serves and accepts the login regardless, so it is not listed as an alternate — check-origins appends the www twin itself.

Stood up 2026-09-22 per process 21-instatic-staging-clone. PUBLIC_ORIGIN is the staging host ALONE, set with skipDeploys before anything could deploy, because a duplicated environment is born holding production's list. The Railway service domain it minted (brandklout-staging.up.railway.app) was DELETED: it bypasses Cloudflare, so no edge rule can de-index it. One door only. Cloudflare response-header rule 1d696d05809041c386b3f328ab0265fb sets X-Robots-Tag noindex, nofollow on this host, and emitCanonical is OFF on its Open Graph plugin - noindex plus a canonical at production is the one pairing Google can resolve against production. There is no www twin and there must not be one.

Cut over 2026-09-11 ~21:40Z. Its PUBLIC_ORIGIN is the staging host ALONE and its generated Railway host was deleted on purpose: that host bypasses Cloudflare and so cannot carry the X-Robots-Tag noindex rule that keeps staging out of Google. One door, de-indexed at the edge.

Added 2026-08-31, the day the rebuilt site was imported (54 pages). The service domain was generated from the IMAGE name (corebunchinstaticlatest-production-fb3b) and was renamed the same day to match the convention the other two sites use. Renaming a service domain silently invalidates PUBLIC_ORIGIN, which is the 403-on-login trap this module exists for, so the order was: widen PUBLIC_ORIGIN to hold BOTH hosts, confirm the container had actually applied it, rename, then narrow it back to the new host alone. pediatricdentistkatytx.com is still on SiteGround DNS and 301s to the parent practice's now-dead mason-park.up.railway.app; when it moves to Cloudflare and points here, add apex AND www to PUBLIC_ORIGIN and re-run the checker BEFORE sending anyone the link. 2026-09-14: the site's domain became masonparkpediatricdental.com (Squarespace registrar, Cloudflare DNS). Apex and www added in Railway, PUBLIC_ORIGIN = www, apex, railway host; redeployed; all three verified OK live. Same day: the new design is not ready for production, so it moved to staging.masonparkpediatricdental.com (now first in PUBLIC_ORIGIN, verified OK). Later still: apex/www now serve the static copy of the old WordPress site from Cloudflare Pages (project mason-park-kids-wp), so they were removed from Railway and from PUBLIC_ORIGIN, which is now staging then the railway host. The apex has no Instatic admin any more.

A generated domain is derived from the service name at creation, so naming afterwards leaves the origin pointing at the old host and every admin write answers 403. There is no client domain yet; when one is bought, follow the cutover in this module and keep the railway host in PUBLIC_ORIGIN — INSTATIC_BASE_URL points at it.
